title: Virtual Networks, Peering, Routes and Public IPs

header.html: Create and configure virtual networks and subnets; create and configure virtual network peering; configure public IP addresses; configure user-defined network routes; troubleshoot network connectivity
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Virtual networks and subnets

An Azure virtual network (VNet) is your private network in Azure. It has one or more address spaces (CIDR ranges such as 10.0.0.0/16) divided into subnets.

Fact Detail
Scope A VNet lives in one region and one subscription
Subnets Each subnet is a range inside the address space; resources get private IPs from it
Reserved addresses Azure reserves 5 addresses in every subnet (network, gateway, two for DNS, broadcast)
Default Resources in a VNet can talk to each other, and outbound internet works by default
Special subnets GatewaySubnet (VPN/ExpressRoute gateway), AzureBastionSubnet, AzureFirewallSubnet

Exam tip

. Address spaces of peered or connected VNets must not overlap. Plan CIDR ranges before you build.

2Virtual network peering

Peering connects two VNets so they communicate over the Microsoft backbone with low latency, as if they were one network.

Fact Detail
Types VNet peering (same region) and global VNet peering (different regions)
Direction Create a peering in both directions (each VNet has a link to the other)
Overlap Address spaces must not overlap
Transitive Not transitive: if A peers with B and B with C, A cannot reach C unless peered directly (or traffic is routed through a network virtual appliance or gateway)
Gateway transit One VNet can share its VPN gateway with a peer (Allow gateway transit and Use remote gateways)
Exam tip

. Peering is not transitive. "A and C cannot communicate through B" is the typical trap.

3Public IP addresses

Setting Options
SKU Basic (being retired [Verify live]) and Standard (zone-redundant, secure by default: closed to inbound traffic until an NSG allows it)
Assignment Static (address does not change) or Dynamic (can change when the resource is deallocated; Basic only)
Attach to NIC of a VM, load balancer frontend, NAT gateway, Bastion, VPN gateway

Standard public IPs and Standard load balancers must match SKUs.

4Routes

Azure has system routes by default (within the VNet, to the internet, between peered VNets). Override them with a route table of user-defined routes (UDRs) associated to subnets.

Item Detail
Address prefix The destination (for example 0.0.0.0/0)
Next hop type Virtual appliance (give its IP), Virtual network gateway, Virtual network, Internet, None (drops traffic)
Use Force traffic through a firewall or network virtual appliance; block a destination with next hop None
Most specific route wins (longest prefix match); a UDR beats a system route with the same prefix

5Troubleshooting connectivity

Tool (Azure Network Watcher) Answers
IP flow verify Is this packet allowed or denied by an NSG rule (and which rule)?
Next hop Where does traffic from this VM go next?
Connection troubleshoot Can A reach B, and where does it fail?
Effective security rules / effective routes The combined rules and routes that apply to a NIC
Topology / packet capture / NSG flow logs Visualize, capture, log traffic
Exam tip

. "Why can't this VM reach that endpoint?" = check effective routes, effective security rules, IP flow verify and next hop.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1VNet A is peered with VNet B, and B with VNet C. Can a VM in A reach a VM in C?

  • AYes, automatically
  • BNo, peering is not transitive
  • COnly with a public IP
  • DOnly in the same subscription
Show the answer

Answer: B. Peering is not transitive; A and C need their own peering or routing.

S2Which requirement must be true to peer two VNets?

  • AThey must use the same subnet names
  • BThey must be in the same resource group
  • CThey must have public IPs
  • DTheir address spaces must not overlap
Show the answer

Answer: D. Overlapping address spaces cannot be peered.

S3All outbound traffic from a subnet must go through a firewall appliance. What should be configured?

  • AA resource lock on the route table so that its routes cannot be changed
  • BA budget alert that fires when outbound data transfer grows too large
  • CA user-defined route with next hop type Virtual appliance
  • DA tag on the subnet that marks it as requiring firewall inspection
Show the answer

Answer: C. UDRs override system routes to force traffic through an appliance.

S4How many IP addresses does Azure reserve in each subnet?

  • A2
  • B10
  • C0
  • D5
Show the answer

Answer: D. Azure reserves five addresses per subnet.

S5An administrator wants to know whether a network security group is blocking traffic to a VM. Which Network Watcher tool fits?

  • AAzure Advisor
  • BIP flow verify
  • CCost analysis
  • DSoft delete
Show the answer

Answer: B. IP flow verify shows whether a packet is allowed or denied and by which rule.

S6A Standard SKU public IP is attached to a VM. What is its default inbound behavior?

  • AClosed until an NSG allows traffic
  • BOpen to all traffic
  • COpen only to Azure services
  • DOpen only for RDP
Show the answer

Answer: A. Standard public IPs are secure by default.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the largest unit of a VNet's address plan?

Show the answer

The address space (CIDR range).

R2Is VNet peering transitive?

Show the answer

No.

R3How many peering links does a full peering need?

Show the answer

Two, one in each direction.

R4What is a UDR?

Show the answer

A user-defined route in a route table that overrides system routes.

R5Which next hop type drops traffic?

Show the answer

None.

R6Which tool shows the next hop for traffic from a VM?

Show the answer

Network Watcher next hop.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
VNet one region; subnets; 5 reserved addresses; special subnets
Peering both directions; no overlap; not transitive; global peering across regions
Public IP Standard (secure by default, zone-redundant) vs Basic; static or dynamic
Routes UDR with next hop; longest prefix wins; UDR beats system route
Troubleshoot IP flow verify, next hop, connection troubleshoot, effective rules and routes
